flags.water-sewer: Whether this lot has water and sewer service available is currently unknown and hasn't been scored [utilities.water_sewer]. You should request a PWSA availability letter to confirm this before moving forward [utilities.water_sewer].
flags.adu: Under a PROPOSED rule (Bill 2025-1545, held in council with a hearing set for 2026-09-23) the site's RM-M zoning could allow up to 2 accessory dwelling units by right, each up to 1,000 sq ft and 30 ft tall, without needing the owner to live there — but this is not law yet [zoning.district, reform.status].
flags.parking-minimum: Also under this PROPOSED bill, off-street parking minimums (required parking spaces) could be eliminated, which may free up land and money for more housing instead — but again, this is not law yet [reform.status].
flags.affordable-housing-bonus: The PROPOSED bill also includes an optional Affordable Housing Bonus that could apply here since the parcel is outside the Inclusionary Housing Overlay, though this bonus is not law yet [overlay.iz, reform.status].
flags.gap-financing: This parcel is in a neighborhood with a low median assessed land value, which often means additional 'gap' financing is needed to make a project pencil out; this is just a note, not a penalty on the score [hood.median_land_psf].
flags.phfa-infill: Because this is a vacant lot in a low-value area, it may qualify for infill or blight-related scoring under PHFA (Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency) programs, but you should confirm this against PHFA's current criteria [landuse.vacant, hood.median_land_psf].
flags.public-owner: The parcel is owned by the City, which may make it easier (though not guaranteed) to acquire through a public disposition process [owner.type].
